mismatch.message: pickup() requiring a partial or failed lift

summary: The admitted 5000-arrow pickup reaches JS preflightPickupObjects, which refuses stacks requiring a partial lift before the existing carry_count/lift_object path can compute and offer the C-selected quantity.

source.branch: The pickup command selects the floor stack, pickup_object calls lift_object, and lift_object stores carry_count’s returned quantity before offering the burden prompt. carry_count computes a partial count for a stack whose full weight exceeds max_capacity, emits the partial-lift line, restores object fields, and returns the count.
callers: hack.c:dopickup calls pickup(-count) after pickup_checks; the admitted comma command uses this production route.
pickup.c:pickup walks the selected floor objects and calls pickup_object in source order.
pickup.c:pickup_object observes the object and consumes lift_object’s return before calling pick_obj.
dependencies: pickup.c:carry_count returns a quantity consumed by pickup.c:lift_object. The corresponding JS helper is implemented and scripts/pickup.test.mjs pins its partial and zero-lift messages.
pickup.c:lift_object writes the adjusted count returned by carry_count and may ask the burden prompt before pickup_object reaches pick_obj.
pickup.c:pickup_object calls lift_object and only extracts/adds the object after a positive result.
JS preflightPickupObjects is an additional admission/planning layer; its UnsupportedPickupError for partial-or-failed lifts blocks those existing source owners.

evidence: Saved v56 admission evaluation challenges/evaluations/admission-398f9e5f3ced1ce3a9ae82d58b56494fe09c5fd6-v56.json at 398f9e5f3ced1ce3a9ae82d58b56494fe09c5fd6 is tied to manifest digest a05e102b18a6c939cbe407c82a83d058037489ba53df8cab9ee52a2568727d74 and recording digest c11c14255290244d40202a68feb314faba8b6ff81a0d0d5936e5a1b5df8d412a; this case has 77/98 matched screens and cursors, 2975/2981 RNG, runner error null, and 21 remaining screens.

A selected-case diagnostic at execution commit e8f757faa235cac634efac291cb0622a527e215f stops at command step 77 with the boundary “unsupported pickup: pickup() requiring a partial or failed lift”; the mismatch is a deliberate preflight refusal, not a runner exception.

The recorded C path emits “You can only lift some of the 5000 arrows lying here.” at step 77, then asks “You have extreme difficulty lifting 1859 arrows. Continue? [ynq] (q)” at step 78. The subsequent input accepts the pickup and reaches normal turn processing.

nethack-c/upstream/src/hack.c:dopickup routes the comma command through pickup(-count). pickup.c:672-910 selects the floor object and calls pickup_object; pickup.c:1803-1892 calls lift_object; pickup.c:1705-1794 consumes carry_count’s returned count and handles the burden prompt; pickup.c:1570-1701 computes partial stack quantity and prints the corresponding message.

js/pickup.js:preflightPickupObjects currently throws “pickup() requiring a partial or failed lift” whenever its aggregate weight estimate exceeds the threshold except a one-item zero-lift case. That guard runs before js/pickup.js:pickup_object -> lift_object -> carry_count can produce C’s partial quantity. The whole carry_count implementation is already pinned by scripts/pickup.test.mjs: carry_count prints both C partial-lift and zero-lift branches.
